gap: No result ChatGPT got says that LiTime's self-heating pads turn on only while a LiFePO4 charger is connected, supplying 14.2–14.6 V and more than 20 A for a 200Ah battery (more than 15 A for a 100Ah). LiTime also says the battery does not charge while it is heating. So a parked RV with no charger, or a small solar controller, never warms the battery and never charges it below 41°F.
standout_why: I compared three pages. BatteryTrail's spec database (cited) lists only 'Self-heating: Yes/No' and the cutoff temperatures. It says nothing about what powers the heater or what turns it on. BoondockMaps (cited) says Epoch 'warms the cells so charging continues down to -4F' but gives no trigger condition. VanPowerCalc (cited) says the heater 'draws 25-75Wh from the pack', which is the opposite of LiTime's plug-in rule. None of the three gives a minimum charger current or voltage for heating. None separates the old charger-only heaters from LiTime's newer LiHeat 'Dual-Mode' line, which can preheat on battery power.
decides: This changes ChatGPT's 'best for cold weather on a budget' pick, the LiTime 12V 200Ah Plus Self-Heating. That battery heats only from a charger that pushes more than 20 A at 14.2–14.6 V. A 10–15 A converter or a small solar MPPT will not trigger it, and an RV in storage gets no heat at all. For winter boondocking, a LiTime LiHeat Dual-Mode model ('preheat with battery power before charging') fits better. If your charging source can't reach 20 A, buy a cutoff-only battery and keep it warm yourself, for example the LiTime 230Ah (32°F charge off, 41°F resume). Battle Born's heated BB10012H also heats only with a charge source present, but it powers the roughly 28 W heater from its own cells. So it needs a charger present but not a 20 A one.

findings.label: Charger needed to start heating
findings.value: DC charger at 14.2–14.6 V and more than 15 A (100Ah) or more than 20 A (200Ah)
findings.source_title: LiTime Self-Heating vs Low Temperature Protection Series
findings.note: This is Step 1 of LiTime's heating procedure. Heating is described only as happening during charging, and the page describes no heating without a charger.

findings.label: Heating window and behaviour
findings.value: Heats when the battery is between -4°F and 41°F (-20°C and 5°C) and stops at 50°F (10°C). The battery does not charge during heating. Warm-up takes about 90 min from 14°F and about 150 min from -4°F.
findings.source_title: LiTime Self-Heating vs Low Temperature Protection Series
findings.note: The same page also gives a shorter range in Step 3: 30–60 min from 14°F and 70–100 min from -4°F. The cutoff-only series stops charging below 32°F (0°C) and resumes at 41°F (5°C) after the user warms the battery.
